turns.speaker: host
turns.text: At Punta Lobos the broken wall of Hotel San Cristóbal rests on the sand.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: La Nigua says inspectors from Profepa checked the site on 11 November.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: They found no waste in the sea, yet the rubble stays under watch.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Fishers had warned about the waves long before any collapse.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The Tres Santos project reported the wall collapse and took down the damaged sections.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: No wildlife was hurt, and no chemicals reached the water.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Still the debris sits there under careful eyes.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The sea keeps coming in at the same edge where the hotel once stood.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: This is Radio BCS2050. Today a deep dive on Development. What holds the edge of a town when the sea takes its share?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: La Nigua reports that on 11 November Profepa inspected the Hotel San Cristóbal site in Punta Lobos after a wall collapse in the Tres Santos project.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What did they find?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: No wastewater or chemicals reached the sea, and no wildlife was harmed. They will now check the environmental permit and how the debris is handled.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. A wall falls and suddenly the sea is part of the story.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: NTCD says the Fifth Government Report covering 1 Sep 2025 to 31 Aug 2026 was delivered to Congress on 12 November. The governor presents it publicly on 27 November at Plaza de la Reforma in La Paz.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What does the report actually track?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Works and actions grouped under the five axes of the State Development Plan.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And the people who live with those axes every day?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Meganoticias reports Los Cabos business owners say the state has paused the Camina Cabo walkability plan and the downtown Cabo San Lucas makeover, even though Fiturca funds were ready.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Why pause it?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: No explanation given. Shops are closing and moving to El Tezal.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: A plan meant to bring people downtown now keeps them away.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The same outlet notes that 704 homes in Sierra Vista are over 90 percent built to move families out of stream beds. More than 17,000 homes are assigned across Los Cabos, but land and drinking water remain the main obstacles.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What happens to the families still waiting?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Luz, the numbers from Los Cabos keep pointing somewhere deeper.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Gringo Gazette reports the 2027 revenue law at 6,746 million pesos, down nine percent. Own-source revenue falls nearly 20% from property tax and fees.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That drop sits right next to the coastal road fight and the estuary cleanup.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Diario Humano notes residents will collect signatures 19 to 22 November under The Coastal Road stays. Noticabo says the Fonatur plant move aims to restore the San José estuary with new pumping stations.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. And the Oasis tender brings 72 megawatts of solar plus hydrogen storage.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: PVTIME reports the project would serve 40,000 households and cut 94,000 tonnes of CO2. Meanwhile the forum in Los Cabos pushes for a five-state treaty to guide investment and conservation.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So the thread runs through water, power, and the coastline itself. The portal's earlier Foresight already flagged water scarcity as the brake on tourism growth.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Meganoticias adds Shell Nurse artificial reefs in La Paz Bay, a fisheries response to warming waters with cost-benefit work by the IDB.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Yet the same week the forum calls for tripling investment across the region, fishers at Punta Lobos are still waiting for a technical report on why the hotel foundations washed out.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: HOY BCS says waves exposed the building after the seawall failed. The surprise is how the push for roads, ports and solar can run ahead of the simple question of where the sand goes next.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What does that tell us about the real limits the desert and the tide set on any plan?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Did you know Baja California Sur grew at 2.1 percent a year over the last decade?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That number comes from the Sea of Cortez Forum in Los Cabos.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Two point one percent. What does that pace feel like on the ground?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: IMCO reports the state climbed from eighth to fifth in competitiveness between 2021 and 2026.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: A quiet climb. Yet the same forum proposed 3.5 percent annual growth for 20 years.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: With roads, ports and airports to support it.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So the road south carries both the past pace and the new ambition.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Agustín Coppel also spoke of tripling regional foreign direct investment from its current level near 4.1 billion dollars. Hans Herrmann suggested a five-state treaty to handle the shared sea and its limits. In Los Cabos the same growth engine meets water scarcity that already slows new hotels and sends residents marching for answers.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal’s Visión pillar for housing points to one clear risk.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Homes built without services or on the coast and over stressed water.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: State population stands at 798,447 from the 2020 census. This week the housing beat is quiet. Housing shows zero items against the EWMA of 1.46, direction flat.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So the aspiration stays simple.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Housing that sits inside real water and energy margins and away from the first line of risk. No published 2050 unit target exists.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What would it take to steer toward the polycentric picture the portal describes?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Each place keeps its own role. Los Cabos stays the stressed tourism engine. La Paz holds the service and water-energy node. Comondú grows food and power without draining its towns or protected zones. East Cape stays in tension with its protected areas. Todos Santos and El Pescadero form the Pacific amenity spine. Loreto anchors tourism and conservation. Northern Mulegé holds the thin corridor with its new remote generation tender.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. The desert light still falls differently on each of those spines.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: New growth only where the demand-supply board shows margin or non-DMA supply. East Cape and Loreto stay inside their ANP and POEL limits first.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The levers are already there.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Prioritise moving what is already exposed before any new coastal front opens. Cross-check every project against the board and the planning instruments. Treat the backlog of missing services as a hard ceiling.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And if those conditions hold, the state keeps its distinct pieces instead of one repeated coastal line from south to north.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That is the reading the portal’s demand-supply board still summarises as constrained at state scale.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The lesson is simple. Homes with services, off the first line of risk, and inside the real margin of water and energy. The kind of housing that respects the desert's limits and the sea's reach.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Mm. And 704 of those homes are planned in Sierra Vista to move families out of danger zones in Los Cabos.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: But here's the thing. Part of Hotel San Cristóbal in Punta Lobos was already taken by the waves. Fishers had warned about the risks, and now debris is being watched so it does not reach the sea.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Los Cabos projects a 9% drop in 2027 revenue as the real estate market cools. Business owners say the Camina Cabo walkability plan has been paused.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Residents are gathering signatures to keep the East Cape Coastal Road in the 2040 urban plan. What does the coast teach us about where we build?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Stay with us. More Radio BCS2050 after the music.
